issues.title: Does Gmail read OTP-Token today, and what makes a sender eligible for the Copy code card?
issues.author: VXNCXNX
issues.body:
We added `OTP-Token: "123456"; origin="https://preuve.ai"` to our sign-in emails (Amazon SES, header arrives byte for byte, SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass).

Gmail (Android, iOS, web) never shows the Copy code card for us. Tested on 2026-10-27:
- 4 and 6 digit codes, with and without OTP-Token
- a minimal code-only email
- X's own verification email resent byte for byte from our domain, only the code changed (X's original gets the card and has no OTP-Token header)
- a fresh code-only sender address

Same content gets the card from X and not from us, so it looks sender-based.

Questions:
1. Does Gmail consume OTP-Token yet, or is it planned?
2. Is there a sender eligibility rule (reputation, volume, registration) senders can meet?
3. Should OTP-Token origin binding require DKIM alignment (Open Question 3)? We would sign it if that is the plan.

Happy to run tests if useful.
